title: Projective complexes and their set and cohomology-sheaf model localizations
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small category with a Grothendieck topology $J$ given by covering sieves: a sieve is a set of arrows into an object closed under precomposition, the maximal sieve covers, and covering sieves satisfy pullback stability and transitivity. No fibre products or subcanonicity are assumed. Use [def-weil-size-convention] for universes and [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] for associated sheaves.

Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring, $\mathcal P=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}},\operatorname{Mod}_\Lambda)$, and $\mathsf M=\operatorname{Ch}(\mathcal P)$ the unbounded cochain complexes [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $W_{\mathrm{obj}}$ be objectwise quasi-isomorphisms and $W_J$ the maps inducing isomorphisms on all cohomology presheaves after module sheafification. Use the enhanced localization and mapping spaces of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. A model category is complete and cocomplete, with retract-closed weak equivalences satisfying two-out-of-three and two weak factorization systems (cofibrations, trivial fibrations) and (trivial cofibrations, fibrations), admitting functorial factorizations; trivial means also a weak equivalence. A weak factorization system consists of two classes mutually characterized by the diagonal lifting property and a factorization of every map into those two classes. Combinatorial has the meaning of [lem-coef-combinatorial-localization-presentability]. Left proper means that pushout along a cofibration preserves weak equivalences. Fibrant means that the map to the terminal object is a fibration. A Quillen adjunction $L\dashv R$ means that $L$ preserves cofibrations and trivial cofibrations, equivalently that $R$ preserves fibrations and trivial fibrations. A Quillen autoequivalence here means an autoequivalence whose functor and inverse preserve cofibrations and weak equivalences.

There is a left proper combinatorial projective model structure on $\mathsf M$, with weak equivalences $W_{\mathrm{obj}}$, fibrations the objectwise degreewise surjections, and cofibrations the maps with the left lifting property against the objectwise surjective quasi-isomorphisms. Its homotopy function complexes are the coherent mapping spaces in $\mathbf D(\mathcal P)=\mathsf M[W_{\mathrm{obj}}^{-1}]_\infty$. Every object is projectively fibrant. Integer cochain shifts are Quillen autoequivalences of this model.

There is also a combinatorial model structure $\mathsf M_J$ on the same category, with the same cofibrations and weak equivalences exactly $W_J$; the identity $\mathsf M\to\mathsf M_J$ is left Quillen. This assertion specifies no hypercover description of its fibrant objects or of its weak equivalences.

For every small set $B$ of complex maps, the left Bousfield model localization $\mathsf M_B$ exists. Its cofibrations are those of $\mathsf M$; its fibrant objects are precisely the projectively fibrant objects $Z$ such that $\operatorname{Map}^h(b,Z)$ is an equivalence for every $b\in B$; and its weak equivalences $W_B$ are precisely the maps $f$ such that $\operatorname{Map}^h(f,Z)$ is an equivalence for every such $Z$. The homotopy function complexes in this definition are computed in the original projective model, hence in $\mathbf D(\mathcal P)$. The identity $\mathsf M\to\mathsf M_B$ is left Quillen, and $\mathsf M_B$ admits functorial fibrant replacement and both model factorizations. If $B$ is invariant under all integer shifts up to objectwise quasi-isomorphism, each integer shift is a Quillen autoequivalence of $\mathsf M_B$. If every member of $B$ belongs to $W_J$, the identity $\mathsf M_B\to\mathsf M_J$ is left Quillen and $W_B\subseteq W_J$.

source.place: Choudhury--Gallauer, Homotopy theory of dg sheaves, Corollary 3.1, Definition 5.9, Theorem 5.7(1)-(2), Remark 5.8, and the first paragraph before Lemma 5.12, pp. 6, 18-20; the set-localization universal property and shift invariance used in the proofs of Theorems 5.7 and 5.11. No fibrant-object identification from Theorem 5.7(3) or hypercover-generation assertion from Theorem 5.11 is included.

proof.text: Form the small $\mathbf Z$-dg category $\mathcal E$ with objects those of $\mathcal C$ and $\mathcal E(c,d)=\bigoplus_{\mathcal C(d,c)}\Lambda[0]$, composition induced by composition in $\mathcal C$ and multiplication in $\Lambda$. A dg functor $\mathcal E\to\operatorname{Ch}(\mathbf Z)$ is exactly a presheaf of complexes of $\Lambda$-modules: the endomorphism $\lambda\,1_c$ supplies scalar multiplication, and the basis arrows supply the contravariant restriction maps. This identifies its ordinary category with $\mathsf M$. Apply the enriched projective-diagram theorem with $\mathcal N=\operatorname{Ch}(\mathbf Z)$, for which that theorem explicitly verifies every hypothesis, including tensor-cell acyclicity. It gives a locally presentable cofibrantly generated projective model, objectwise quasi-isomorphisms and degreewise surjections, the stated lifting characterization of cofibrations, and functorial factorizations. Write $R_c(T)=\Lambda[\mathcal C(T,c)]$. Its generating cofibrations are $R_c\otimes(S^{n+1}\mathbf Z\to D^n\mathbf Z)$ and its generating trivial cofibrations are $0\to R_c\otimes D^n\mathbf Z$. These are small sets since $\mathcal C$ is small and $n\in\mathbf Z$. Notice that $\Lambda$ need not be projective over $\mathbf Z$: only the unrestricted diagram-model existence part of the cited theorem is used, not its conditional evaluation-preserves-cofibrations clause.

source.place: Fact 2.3, Corollary 3.1, Definition 3.2 and Fact 3.3; agent specialization through the free Lambda-linear dg category

proof.text: Every projective cofibration is a degreewise split monomorphism of presheaves. Indeed factor it by the cellular small-object theorem using the generating cofibrations of step 1. Its right factor is a trivial fibration, so the lifting property makes the original cofibration an arrow retract of the cellular left factor. In each degree a pushout of a coproduct of generating maps adds a direct sum of the presheaves $R_c$ to the source. At a limit ordinal the resulting degree is the source plus the direct sum of all complements added earlier; hence the transfinite composite is split injective in that degree. A retract of a split injection is split injective, by composing the splitting with the retract maps. This proves the claim without any assertion that evaluation preserves cofibrations over $\mathbf Z$.

source.place: Fact 3.11; cellular proof of the degreewise split-injection part

proof.text: The projective model is left proper. Given a pushout of a quasi-isomorphism $X\to Y$ along a cofibration $X\hookrightarrow X'$, step 2 gives degreewise short exact rows $0\to X\to X'\to Q\to0$ and $0\to Y\to Y\amalg_X X'\to Q\to0$. Evaluate at any object of $\mathcal C$, apply the long exact cohomology sequences, their cited naturality for the displayed morphism of short exact sequences, and the five lemma: the maps on the outside terms are the given cohomology isomorphisms and the identity of $H^*(Q)$, so $X'\to Y\amalg_X X'$ is a quasi-isomorphism objectwise. Every object is fibrant since $K\to0$ is degreewise surjective. The functors $[r]$ and $[-r]$ preserve degreewise surjections and quasi-isomorphisms ($H^n(K[r])=H^{n+r}(K)$), and preserve cofibrations by the following lifting calculation. Given a square from $i[r]$ to an objectwise surjective quasi-isomorphism $p$, apply $[-r]$ to obtain a square from $i$ to $p[-r]$. The latter is again an objectwise surjective quasi-isomorphism, so the cofibration $i$ gives a lift; applying $[r]$ gives a lift in the original square. Replacing $r$ by $-r$ proves the assertion for the inverse shift, hence the projective shift assertion.

source.place: Corollary 3.1 and Fact 3.11; long exact sequences: Stacks Tag 0117 (homology-lemma-long-exact-sequence-cochain); five lemma: Tag 05QB (homology-lemma-five-lemma)

proof.text: For the model of step 1 choose cofibrant replacements and cosimplicial frames. The frame-mapping theorem identifies their homotopy function complexes naturally with mapping spaces in the coherent localization at $W_{\mathrm{obj}}$. This is precisely $\mathbf D(\mathcal P)$ with the enhancement in the statement; no passage to only $H^0$ or to ordinary Hom-set orthogonality is being made.

source.place: Lemma 3.16 and the general cosimplicial-frame comparison; no simplicial enrichment is assumed

proof.text: Let $\mathcal A$ be the category of sieve sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules. The sieve-sheafification theorem provides an exact left adjoint $a:\mathcal P\to\mathcal A$, identifying sheaves with modules over the associated constant sheaf of rings. Thus $aH^n(K)=H^n(aK)$, since an exact functor preserves kernels, images and cokernels. The sieve-module-sheaf theorem makes $\mathcal A$ Grothendieck, hence locally presentable. The small-product theorem makes $\mathcal A^{\mathbf Z}$ locally presentable. In $\mathcal P$ filtered colimits and exactness are objectwise; filtered colimits of $\Lambda$-modules are exact by the module Grothendieck theorem. Apply such a colimit to $0\to Z^nK\to K^n\to B^{n+1}K\to0$ and $0\to B^nK\to Z^nK\to H^nK\to0$. Exactness makes $\operatorname{colim}B^{n+1}K\to\operatorname{colim}K^{n+1}$ injective, so the first sequence identifies $\operatorname{colim}Z^nK$ with the kernel of the differential on $\operatorname{colim}K$. The first sequence in degree $n-1$ identifies $\operatorname{colim}B^nK$ with its degree-$n$ boundaries. The second sequence therefore identifies $H^n(\operatorname{colim}K)$ with $\operatorname{colim}H^nK$. Since $a$ is a left adjoint, the functor $H:\mathsf M\to\mathcal A^{\mathbf Z}$, $K\mapsto(aH^nK)_n$, preserves filtered colimits. All assertions here use covering sieves, not fibre products in the site or subcanonicity.

source.place: Definition 5.6 and Remark 5.8; agent accessibility argument using exact sheafification and AB5; Stacks Tag 00DB (algebra-lemma-directed-colimit-exact) for coefficient modules

proof.text: The class $W_J$ is an accessible full subcategory of the arrow category of $\mathsf M$. Put $\mathcal D=\mathcal A^{\mathbf Z}$. Apply the ordinary presheaf local-presentability theorem with indexing category $[1]^{\mathrm{op}}$ and coefficient category $\mathcal D$: the latter is locally presentable by step 5 and has pullbacks computed degree by degree because $\mathcal A$ is abelian. Its conclusion makes the arrow category $\mathcal D^{[1]}$ locally presentable. The full subcategory $\operatorname{Iso}(\mathcal D)\subseteq\mathcal D^{[1]}$ is equivalent to $\mathcal D$ by source and $D\mapsto1_D$: every isomorphism $f:D\to E$ is isomorphic as an arrow to $1_D$. Its inclusion preserves all colimits, computed at the two endpoints; in particular a small family generating $\mathcal D$ under sufficiently filtered colimits supplies such a family of identity arrows generating $\operatorname{Iso}(\mathcal D)$, and it is closed under these colimits. Apply accessible arrow inverse image to the filtered-colimit-preserving $H$ of step 5. Its inverse image of $\operatorname{Iso}(\mathcal D)$ is exactly $W_J$, by the definition of $H$.

source.place: Remark 5.8, existence input independent of the hypercover generation theorem; agent Smith-recognition route

proof.text: Write $C$ for the projective cofibrations. The class $C\cap W_J$ is weakly saturated. For a cofibration $i:K\hookrightarrow L$, step 2 and exact sheafification give a short exact sequence of complexes $0\to aK\to aL\to a\operatorname{coker}(i)\to0$. Its long exact sequence says $i\in W_J$ if and only if $a\operatorname{coker}(i)$ is acyclic. Any pushout of $i$ is again a cofibration and monomorphism with the same cokernel, so it remains in $W_J$. For a transfinite composite of such maps, use induction on the ordinal: successor stages compose isomorphisms under $H$, and at a nonzero limit use preservation of filtered colimits by $H$ from step 5. Hence each map from the initial stage remains in $W_J$. Cofibrations are closed under these operations by their lifting characterization: for a transfinite composite construct the lift successively and take the compatible lift at limits. Retracts and identities stay in $C\cap W_J$ by lifting and by the functor $H$. Similarly $W_J$ has two-out-of-three and is retract closed, since isomorphisms do. Finally $W_{\mathrm{obj}}\subseteq W_J$, so every projective trivial fibration lies in $W_J$.

source.place: Definition 5.6 and Remark 5.8; exact-sequence argument using Stacks Tag 0117 (homology-lemma-long-exact-sequence-cochain)

proof.text: Apply Smith recognition to the underlying complete locally presentable category $\mathsf M$, $C$ and $W_J$. The class $C$ is the weakly saturated closure of the small generating cofibrations in step 1: the small-object factorization and retract argument of step 2 give one containment, and the lifting argument in step 7 gives the other. Step 6 verifies accessibility, and step 7 verifies weak saturation of $C\cap W_J$, two-out-of-three and inclusion $C^{\square}\subseteq W_J$. The result is a combinatorial model structure $\mathsf M_J$ with exactly these cofibrations and weak equivalences. Since a projective trivial cofibration belongs to $C\cap W_J$, the identity from the projective model to $\mathsf M_J$ is left Quillen. No description of local fibrant objects, hypercover tests or hypercover generation enters this construction.

source.place: Remark 5.8 and Theorem 5.7(1)-(2), existence part only; agent recognition proof avoiding Theorem 5.11

proof.text: Apply general set Bousfield localization to the left proper combinatorial model obtained in steps 1-3 and to $S=B$. Its unchanged cofibrations, mapping-space definition of local fibrant objects and weak equivalences, left Quillen identity, functorial factorizations and fibrant replacement are exactly the assertions about $\mathsf M_B$. The homotopy function complexes here are those of the original model, identified in step 4. This use does not require $B$ to consist of cofibrations or have cofibrant endpoints.

source.place: Definition 5.9 and paragraph before Lemma 5.12; general existence theorem of Barwick 4.7

proof.text: Assume $B$ is invariant under every shift up to objectwise quasi-isomorphism of arrows. In $\mathbf D(\mathcal P)$, the inverse equivalences $[r]$ and $[-r]$ give $\operatorname{Map}^h(b,Z[r])\simeq\operatorname{Map}^h(b[-r],Z)$. Replacing an arrow by a zigzag of commuting squares with objectwise quasi-isomorphism vertical components preserves this test, since those components become equivalences. The assumption on $B$ therefore makes its local objects invariant under $[r]$ and $[-r]$. For $f\in W_B$ and local $Z$, the same formula gives $\operatorname{Map}^h(f[r],Z)\simeq\operatorname{Map}^h(f,Z[-r])$, an equivalence. Thus both shifts preserve $W_B$. They already preserve the unchanged cofibrations by step 3, proving the localized shift assertion.

source.place: Definition 5.9 and the shift argument in the proof of Theorem 5.7; explicit mapping-space calculation

proof.text: Suppose $B\subseteq W_J$. For the left Quillen identity $F:\mathsf M\to\mathsf M_J$ of step 8, compute $LF(b)$ by projective cofibrant replacement. The replacement maps lie in $W_{\mathrm{obj}}\subseteq W_J$, so two-out-of-three shows that the replaced arrow $Qb$ belongs to $W_J$ and its image in the homotopy category of $\mathsf M_J$ is invertible. The universal property of general set Bousfield localization now gives the left Quillen identity $\mathsf M_B\to\mathsf M_J$. To get inclusion on all weak equivalences, rather than only those between cofibrant objects, factor any $f\in W_B$ in $\mathsf M_B$ as a cofibration $i$ followed by a trivial fibration $p$. Two-out-of-three makes $i$ a trivial cofibration, hence its image in $\mathsf M_J$ is trivial. The trivial fibrations in both localized models and the original model are exactly $C^{\square}$, because their cofibrations agree; thus $p\in W_{\mathrm{obj}}\subseteq W_J$. Consequently $f=pi\in W_J$, as required.

source.place: Set-localization universal property (Barwick Definition 4.2 and Theorem 4.7), used in Choudhury--Gallauer before Lemma 5.12
